title: I Enforced the Hotel Late Checkout Rule on the Front Desk Manager

parts.text: I asked for a noon checkout at 8:11 a.m. because my train was at 1:40. The front desk manager, Craig, tapped a sign: LATE CHECKOUT $75 — MANAGER APPROVAL ONLY. He approved it, took seventy-five dollars, and smiled like he had invented noon. I was thirty-nine, rolling a suitcase with a broken wheel that clicked on the marble. At 11:52 housekeeping knocked. "We're turning the room. Manager said standard is eleven." I showed the folio. Craig had already posted the fee and then marked the room as eleven anyway. My keycard died in the elevator on the way back from ice. I went to the desk with the folio and the dead card. Craig said, "We needed the room for a VIP." The VIP was his cousin, sitting on a lobby sofa with a rolling bag that did not click. I asked for the manager-on-duty log. Craig said he was the only manager. Then the printer spat out a second folio that still had my seventy-five dollars and a new line: KEY REPLACEMENT $25.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He charged late checkout, evicted me early, and added a key fee while his cousin waited.

social.video_title: He sold me noon and took the room at eleven — Part 1/2
social.description: Seventy-five dollars for noon, a dead keycard, and a VIP who was the manager's cousin. Would you have paid the extra twenty-five?

parts.text: I asked corporate chat on the card of the stand in the lobby. The agent asked Craig to read the timestamps. Housekeeping's eleven knock sat next to a paid noon flag. Craig's cousin stood up and left without a reservation appearing in the system. Corporate reversed both fees and comped a night I will never use in that building. Craig said I had embarrassed the property. I said the property had sold a time it did not have. I rolled my clicking suitcase to the station at 12:20 with a working paper receipt. The review I left quoted the sign: MANAGER APPROVAL ONLY. He had approved it. He had also voided it. I ate a station pretzel and watched the train board. Noon still exists. It just does not live at that desk.

social.video_title: Corporate read the timestamps he hoped nobody would — Part 2/2
social.description: Paid noon, eleven knock, cousin with no reservation. Both fees reversed. Was VIP ever a policy?
